currentContext.business: The Company manufactures a focused portfolio of value-added coated steel - Alu-Zinc coated steel and pre-painted steel coils and sheets - from its flagship Kutch, Gujarat facility, serving customers in construction, white goods, home appliances, automotive and general engineering. It became an independent entity from the Manaksia Group in 2010 and sells across India, Europe, Africa and other global markets, with an export footprint spanning more than 22 countries supported by branch offices, stockyards and service centres nationwide. A separate Bhopal facility in Madhya Pradesh operates under a contract-manufacturing arrangement producing Ultramarine Blue Powder for FMCG use.

Pre-Painted Steel: Colour Strong - flagship pre-painted steel brand on an ISO 9001-certified colour-coating process, for roofing, cladding and architectural applications
Alu-Zinc Steel: Zingalvo - hot-dip galvanised Alu-Zinc coated steel brand, used as a finished product or as a base substrate for downstream coating/painting
Galvanised Corrugated (GC) Steel: Singham - high-strength Galvanised Corrugated steel brand at an accessible price point for everyday structural needs
FMCG contract manufacturing: Ultramarine Blue Powder (Bhopal plant, contract-manufacturing arrangement)

currentContext.end_markets: Construction|White goods and home appliances|Automotive|General engineering|Infrastructure|FMCG (via contract manufacturing)|India - 20+ states, more than 240 active customers|Exports to more than 22 countries across Europe, Africa and the Middle East

currentContext.strengths: Focused specialisation: rather than pursuing breadth, the Company has deepened expertise in coated steel, building a business defined by technical excellence and agile execution|Structural logistics advantage - Kutch plant located around 50 km from the Kandla and Mundra ports, enabling cost-effective domestic and international dispatch|Proprietary coated-steel brands (Colour Strong, Zingalvo, Singham) developed for distinct market segments|Established export franchise across more than 22 countries with deepening relationships in Europe, Africa and the Middle East, reinforced by long-term supply agreements with marquee European clients|Ability to deliver customised solutions in smaller order quantities without compromising quality or service, combined with strong relationships with global OEMs|Premium product positioning - Alu-Zinc coated steel commands a premium of Rs 3,000 to Rs 5,000 per tonne over conventional galvanised steel|Improving financial profile recognised externally, with Acuite upgrading the long-term rating to A from A- and the short-term rating to A1 from A2|Accredited quality and safety systems (BIS, ISO 9001/14001/45001) supporting export acceptance
currentContext.strategies: Compete on value rather than volume alone - premiumisation is at the core of the strategy, with a portfolio spanning Alu-Zinc coated steel coils and sheets and pre-painted steel coils and sheets|Move up the value chain by shifting sales mix towards pre-painted and Alu-Zinc coated products (pre-painted steel was 80.44% of sales, up from 74.49%)|Expand value-added capacity - second colour coating line and a proposed second Aluminium-Zinc line|Strengthen backward integration through a planned Cold Rolling Mill complex that shifts primary raw material from cold-rolled coil to hot-rolled coil, reducing dependence on a concentrated supplier base|Grow the export franchise, deepening presence in Europe (largest export market) and opening South and Central America on the back of the Alu-Zinc transition|Deliver customised solutions in smaller order quantities and leverage relationships with global OEMs to support realisations and margins|Invest in captive renewable power (7 MW solar) to lower energy cost and carbon footprint, supporting CBAM-exposed export markets|Build digital capability through Salesforce CRM and a Manufacturing Execution System to connect customer demand with shop-floor operations|Disciplined capital allocation with a targeted ROCE of more than 18%, alongside deleveraging (net debt reduced to Rs 81 crores, debt-equity improved to 1.13x from 1.81x)|Vision FY29 - purposeful scale through expanding value-added capacities, improving Alu-Zinc line utilisation and strengthening backward integration|Protect healthy EBITDA margins through market cycles and build a robust order pipeline|Build organisational capability - strengthening the leadership bench with senior steel and manufacturing professionals and expanding sales and marketing teams for the international footprint|The AGM notice places a final dividend of Rs 0.05 per equity share (5% on the Re 1 face value) for the year ended 31st March, 2026 for declaration by members. Beyond this declaration, the governance sections of the report state no dividend, buyback or reinvestment policy; the stated governance intent is prudent financial management practices, professionalism in decision making and enhancing value for stakeholders.|Commissioning a 7 MW captive solar power plant expected to offset 50-55% of grid-power dependency, lowering the carbon footprint and per-unit energy cost, described as consistent with the Company's stated ESG commitment|Investment in renewable captive power positioned as the response to energy-transition and environmental compliance requirements, alongside a Board-level Risk Management Policy covering identification, assessment, mitigation and monitoring of risks
currentContext.expansion: FY26's headline project was the upgradation of the Kutch galvanising line: the Continuous Galvanising Line was converted to an Alu-Zinc Coating Line within a planned 35-day shutdown, with the first coil meeting quality benchmarks without trial losses. Capacity rose from 1,32,000 TPA to 1,80,000 TPA (+36%) and production transitioned to 100% Alu-Zinc, placing the Company among the select Indian manufacturers with complete Alu-Zinc coating capability; the project was commissioned in December 2025. Three growth projects are under implementation. A second colour coating line adds 1,50,000 TPA, taking total colour coating capacity from 86,000 TPA to 2,36,000 TPA (+174%, described elsewhere as 2.7 times) on an approved investment of Rs 65 crore, with commissioning targeted for Q2 FY27 - it removes the bottleneck on an existing line running at 97.2% utilisation. A 7 MW captive solar power project at Kutch, Gujarat, costing Rs 30 crore, is also targeted for Q2 FY27 and is expected to offset around 50%-55% of grid power dependency, cut effective power costs by nearly 40% and generate annual savings of Rs 7 crore to Rs 7.5 crore while supporting lower-CBAM-impact products for Europe. An enterprise-wide Salesforce CRM implementation is in progress. Beyond these, the roadmap is to progress a 3,60,000 MTPA Cold Rolling Mill complex targeted for FY28 at an estimated Rs 200 crore - shifting the primary raw material from cold-rolled coil to hot-rolled coil, incorporating a process acid recycling facility and reducing dependence on a concentrated supplier base - followed by a second Alu-Zinc line, with Alu-Zinc utilisation to be raised to 80%-85% along the way.

risks.note: Fluctuating cold rolled steel, zinc and aluminium prices can influence input spending and margins; mitigated through dynamic pricing, disciplined procurement and planned backward integration into a cold rolling mill.

Rising costs of industrial fuels and petrochemical-based consumables can raise production costs; new pricing is intended to absorb the full incremental cost and a 7 MW captive solar plant is being commissioned to offset 50-55% of grid-power dependency.

Currency fluctuations may impact export outcomes and profitability; the rising export base provides a natural forex inflow and new-contract pricing factors in prevailing currency levels, with exposure monitored on an ongoing basis.

risks.risk: Sustainability and energy transition / environmental compliance
risks.note: Dynamic environmental expectations and energy transition requirements may influence operating costs and compliance obligations; the industry also faces increasing environmental compliance requirements and decarbonisation-related investments across the steel value chain.

risks.risk: Exposure to global steel prices and international trade dynamics
risks.note: Listed among industry market restraints - fluctuations in global steel prices and changing trade patterns affect competitiveness and realisations for a business whose exports are described as a significant pillar of strategy across more than 22 international markets.
High logistics and transportation costs impact supply chain efficiency across the steel industry, relevant to a single-site manufacturer serving both pan-India and export markets.

risks.risk: Global economic uncertainty and geopolitical disruption
risks.note: Geopolitical disruptions affect demand patterns, trade flows and input availability; the Middle East conflict late in the financial year affected energy markets, transportation routes and supply chains, raising production and logistical costs across manufacturing including steel.

risks.risk: Raw material price volatility in the wider steel chain
risks.note: Volatility in iron ore, coking coal and energy input prices affects production costs and profitability across the sector, feeding through to the cold-rolled substrate the Company buys in.

one-line thesis: A clean recovery quarter: after a shutdown-hit H2 FY26, the fully-shifted Alu-Zinc line + fresh orders priced to fully cover post-war costs drove a record EBITDA/ton of Rs 10,400 and margin back to ~11%. The next two quarters are a genuine step-change — the 2nd colour-coating line (+174% pre-painted capacity) and a 7 MW captive solar plant both commission in Q2 FY27 — underpinning a ~Rs 1,300-1,350 cr FY27 revenue guide with structural margin support.
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy):
| Metric | Q1 FY27 | YoY / QoQ | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue (consol) | ₹263 cr | +3.6% YoY / +15% QoQ | Realisation ₹88,597/ton vs ₹79,180 Q4 (+12%) — mix + pricing |
| EBITDA / margin | ₹29.08 cr / 11.06% | +86% QoQ / +422 bps QoQ | EBITDA/ton ₹10,400 — **highest ever** |
| PBT | ₹18.93 cr | +197% QoQ | — |
| PAT / margin | ₹14.10 cr / 5.36% | +163% QoQ / +301 bps QoQ | EPS ₹1.31 (+102% QoQ); cash profit ₹17.40 cr (+115% QoQ) |
| Finance cost | ₹6.86 cr | -11.8% YoY | Good given higher Alu-Zinc asset base |
| Volume | 27,938 MT sales | ~-4% YoY (vs ~29,000) | Pure Alu-Zinc ramp timing; galvanized = 0 |
| Net debt | ~₹115 cr | — | Peak debt seen ₹125-130 cr, not ₹140 cr |
> One-offs / distortions: the YoY volume dip (27,900 vs ~29,000 MT) is "100% attributable" to the Alu-Zinc line still ramping (62% util), not demand. The margin snap-back reflects the shift from Q4's un-passed-through cost spike to Q1 orders priced with a full cost + buffer.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Revenue:** FY27 ~₹1,300-1,350 cr (~150,000 tons at 50-60% util of new capacity); FY28 ~₹1,700-1,750 cr (180,000-200,000 tons). Post-Phase-2 peak revenue ₹2,500-2,700 cr (~3 lakh tons).
- **Margin:** consolidated EBITDA improving toward the top of the 10-12% band; further +1-2% headroom from new capacity + solar + richer mix; EBITDA/ton ₹10,400 "sustainable and due for further growth."
- **Commissioning (Q2 FY27):** 2nd colour-coating line (pre-painted capacity 86k → 236k tons, +174%) AND 7 MW captive solar (offsets 50-55% of Kutch grid power) — both same quarter.
- **Alu-Zinc ramp:** 62% util now → 75-80% in ~3 months.
- **Capex:** Phase 2 (cold-rolling backward integration + 2nd Alu-Zinc line) ~₹350 cr, starts FY28; ₹140 cr already spent (Alu-Zinc upgrade + CCL2 + solar), residual ₹15-20 cr debt; additional ~₹100 cr debt for the full plan; leverage capped ≤1.25x D/E.
- **Order book:** ₹450 cr (±₹20-25 cr), ~4.5-5 months execution; sustainable ₹350-450 cr going forward; incremental EBITDA galv→Alu-Zinc ₹1,000-3,000/ton.
order book & pipeline: Order book ~₹450 cr (≈1.5 quarters), executable in 4.5-5 months; ~80% export-concentrated, largely repeat quarterly orders from long-term European + domestic OEM customers with annual-offtake MoUs. Grown structurally from ₹100-120 cr lows to ₹400-450 cr as delivery capability was proven.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Pre-Painted steel:** 20,510 tons produced at 95.4% util (near-full — demand waiting for CCL2); 74% of sales mix.
- **Alu-Zinc:** 27,941 tons (+8% QoQ) at 62% util; 26% of sales; galvanized fully phased out (0 in Q1).
- **Exports:** 65% of volume = 18,221 MT; pre-painted export volume +25% YoY, export revenue +20% YoY. 4 new markets entered: **Latvia, Brazil, Jamaica, Somalia**.
growth verticals / optionality:
- CCL2 (+174% pre-painted capacity) = the near-term revenue catalyst, ramping through H2 FY27.
- Phase 2: cold-rolling mill (backward integration, FY28) → compresses working-capital cycle from ~75 days toward single-digit days (fewer SKUs to stock).
- 2nd Alu-Zinc line (Phase 2) → peak ~3 lakh tons.
- Americas (South/Central) penetration for premium Alu-Zinc; explicitly avoiding US (trade policy).
6a. moat & competitive position (optiona:
- **Back-to-back model:** finished product sold on advance order book, then raw material procured against orders-in-hand — insulates from commodity price risk (the mechanism behind the Q1 margin recovery).
- **Alu-Zinc premiumisation:** commands ₹1,000-3,000/ton incremental EBITDA over galvanized (both cost savings + product premium).
- **Captive solar (7 MW):** structural, permanent 50-55% grid-power offset at Kutch — a per-unit cost edge peers lack.
margins & cost dynamics:
- EBITDA/ton ₹10,400 (record) on Alu-Zinc mix + higher realisation + full cost pass-through on new orders.
- Q4 FY26 compression was LPG/propane spiking from ₹60/kg → ₹200/kg (Iran war / Hormuz); now cooled to ~₹80/kg (~25% above pre-war). India diversified LPG sourcing (US/Canada/Australia/Venezuela/Russia) + govt LPG→PNG push eased availability.
- Pass-through resets every quarter with fresh export orders; solar to further cut power cost per unit from Q2.
capex / expansion (watch slippage):
- **Q2 FY27:** CCL2 (86k→236k tons pre-painted) + 7 MW solar — both from CWIP, capitalising shortly. Residual debt ₹15-20 cr to deploy.
- **FY28 (Phase 2):** cold-rolling mill + 2nd Alu-Zinc line, ~₹350 cr, funding mix (internal + debt + equity) still being frozen.
- Ramp risk: Alu-Zinc "teething troubles" of a new automated line; CCL2 expected to ramp faster (less complex), 50-60% util in H2 FY27.
capital allocation:
- Debt ~₹115 cr, D/E just above 1x; peak debt guided ₹125-130 cr (repayments already running); leverage cap ≤1.25x for current phase.
- Cash flow directed to capex + working capital for the scale-up; low utilisation of bank WC limits → headroom.
- Target ROCE >20% for new projects (from prior call context).
risks & watch-items:
- **Export concentration** (~80% of order book) — single-geography demand shocks (Europe/Africa) hit hardest.
- **Fuel/import dependence:** LPG/propane price + availability (Hormuz); mitigating via GSPC natural-gas pipeline (agreement in process).
- Execution/ramp risk on CCL2, Alu-Zinc and (later) cold-rolling backward integration.
- Steel commodity-cycle volatility (managed via back-to-back model).
- Working-capital build during the scale-up.
management quality / tone: Confident, detailed, numbers-forward (WTD Karan Agrawal fielded almost all questions with specifics). Careful to separate firm FY27/FY28 guides from "far-fetched" Phase-2 peak numbers ("premature to estimate"). Honest that the YoY volume dip is ramp-timing, and that a precise 12% FY27 margin can't be pinned. Credible on the back-to-back cost-insulation model.
non-obvious takeaways:
- Two independent step-changes (CCL2 + solar) land in the *same* quarter (Q2 FY27) — FY27 is back-half-loaded; H1 optics understate the exit run-rate.
- Cold-rolling backward integration is as much a *working-capital* story (75 days → single digits) as a margin story — under-appreciated cash-flow lever.
- Galvanized is fully gone; the whole book is now Alu-Zinc/pre-painted, so mix-up is structural not cyclical.
- Deliberately skipping the US market (tariff/trade risk) and steering premium Alu-Zinc to South/Central America.

themes.title: Metals & mining cycle - steel, aluminium, critical minerals
themes.need: Domestic demand growth, safeguard duties and an India capacity-expansion wave lift integrated metals while critical-mineral security gains policy support. TATASTEEL targets 45-50 MT India (FY26 India EBITDA INR34,272cr at 24% margin) with a +INR6,000/t 1QFY27 realisation uplift; JINDALSTEL/SAIL/JSWSTEEL-tier on steel; HINDALCO/NALCO on aluminium; HINDZINC on zinc (Q1FY27 all-time-record EBITDA INR8,074cr +109% YoY on a record-low zinc cost-of-production USD851/t, though CEO Arun Misra hands over to ex-SAIL chief Amarendu Prakash 1-Aug-2026 and a new Gundlupet REE/Yttrium critical-minerals block won this quarter is a 2031-32-dated option, not near-term); NMDC/COALINDIA/LLOYDSME/SARDAEN on iron-ore/coal/integrated mining. Q1FY27 also quantified the export-side shock and the downstream escape from it: JINDALSAW's consolidated PAT fell 78% YoY to INR 91cr on +9% revenue because the Strait-of-Hormuz blockade suspended ALL India-origin MENA export shipments from March 2026, holding utilisation at ~60-65%; SHYAMMETL took the other route, posting INR 5,455cr revenue (+23.3%) at a multi-quarter-high 14.9% EBITDA margin with aluminium EBITDA/t +52% YoY and specialty alloys near 20.5% margin, self-funding ~INR 9,580cr of balance capex with no debt.
themes.driver: Steel price/realisation uplift into Q1; safeguard-duty support; Hormuz reopening for line-pipe exports; value-added/downstream mix; iron-ore + critical-mineral volume ramp.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Among India's leading manufacturers and exporters of premium-quality value-added steel products, specialising in pre-painted steel (PPGI/PPGL) and bare Alu-Zinc steel (GL) in coil and sheet formats.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company manufactures a focused portfolio of value-added coated steel - Alu-Zinc coated steel and pre-painted steel coils and sheets - from its flagship Kutch, Gujarat facility, serving customers in construction, white goods, home appliances, automotive and general engineering. It became an independent entity from the Manaksia Group in 2010 and sells across India, Europe, Africa and other global markets, with an export footprint spanning more than 22 countries supported by branch offices, stockyards and service centres nationwide. A separate Bhopal facility in Madhya Pradesh operates under a contract-manufacturing arrangement producing Ultramarine Blue Powder for FMCG use.

Grown structurally from ₹100-120 cr lows to ₹400-450 cr as delivery capability was proven.

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)
guidance.body:
- **Revenue:** FY27 ~₹1,300-1,350 cr (~150,000 tons at 50-60% util of new capacity); FY28 ~₹1,700-1,750 cr (180,000-200,000 tons). Post-Phase-2 peak revenue ₹2,500-2,700 cr (~3 lakh tons).
- **Margin:** consolidated EBITDA improving toward the top of the 10-12% band; further +1-2% headroom from new capacity + solar + richer mix; EBITDA/ton ₹10,400 "sustainable and due for further growth."
- **Commissioning (Q2 FY27):** 2nd colour-coating line (pre-painted capacity 86k → 236k tons, +174%) AND 7 MW captive solar (offsets 50-55% of Kutch grid power) — both same quarter.
- **Alu-Zinc ramp:** 62% util now → 75-80% in ~3 months.
- **Capex:** Phase 2 (cold-rolling backward integration + 2nd Alu-Zinc line) ~₹350 cr, starts FY28; ₹140 cr already spent (Alu-Zinc upgrade + CCL2 + solar), residual ₹15-20 cr debt; additional ~₹100 cr debt for the full plan; leverage capped ≤1.25x D/E.
- **Order book:** ₹450 cr (±₹20-25 cr), ~4.5-5 months execution; sustainable ₹350-450 cr going forward; incremental EBITDA galv→Alu-Zinc ₹1,000-3,000/ton.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- CCL2 (+174% pre-painted capacity) = the near-term revenue catalyst, ramping through H2 FY27.
- Phase 2: cold-rolling mill (backward integration, FY28) → compresses working-capital cycle from ~75 days toward single-digit days (fewer SKUs to stock).
- 2nd Alu-Zinc line (Phase 2) → peak ~3 lakh tons.
- Americas (South/Central) penetration for premium Alu-Zinc; explicitly avoiding US (trade policy).

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's economic growth projected at 6.9% in FY 2026-27, with resilient domestic demand, continued public investment and a gradual recovery in private capex
- Manufacturing sector outlook positive - investments in transportation, urban infrastructure, housing, renewable energy and industrial projects are likely to sustain demand across key steel-consuming sectors
- Demand for coated steel products gaining momentum across construction, industrial and consumer applications
- India's per capita steel consumption at nearly 100 kg remains well below the global average, and the National Steel Policy targets 300 million tonnes of steelmaking capacity by 2030
- Alu-Zinc coated steel gaining wider acceptance for corrosion resistance, finish and service life across construction, appliances, HVAC, clean rooms, sandwich panels, pre-engineered buildings and solar, commanding a premium of Rs 3,000 to Rs 5,000 per tonne over conventional galvanised steel
- India-EU Free Trade Agreement, once implemented, expected to strengthen access to Europe through preferential market access and more favourable quota treatment for FTA partners
- Evolving CBAM requirements make technology, compliance and sustainable manufacturing increasingly important to long-term export competitiveness
- Global steel producers face volatile raw material prices, elevated energy costs and changing trade patterns; focus on value-added products and export diversification remains prominent
- Global GDP growth projected at 3.1% in CY 2026 and 3.2% in CY 2027, with global inflation at 4.4% in CY 2026 indicating persistent near-term cost pressure
- Government measures supporting the sector - PLI for Specialty Steel, the revised DMI&SP Policy, PM GatiShakti logistics integration and FTA-driven market access
- Management states a priority of 'building a robust order pipeline'; no order-book quantum is disclosed in this text
- Export franchise described as serving over 240 active customers across more than 20 Indian states and 22 countries

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body:
- EBITDA/ton ₹10,400 (record) on Alu-Zinc mix + higher realisation + full cost pass-through on new orders.
- Q4 FY26 compression was LPG/propane spiking from ₹60/kg → ₹200/kg (Iran war / Hormuz); now cooled to ~₹80/kg (~25% above pre-war). India diversified LPG sourcing (US/Canada/Australia/Venezuela/Russia) + govt LPG→PNG push eased availability.
- Pass-through resets every quarter with fresh export orders; solar to further cut power cost per unit from Q2.

- Target ROCE >20% for new projects (from prior call context).

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: FY26's headline project was the upgradation of the Kutch galvanising line: the Continuous Galvanising Line was converted to an Alu-Zinc Coating Line within a planned 35-day shutdown, with the first coil meeting quality benchmarks without trial losses. Capacity rose from 1,32,000 TPA to 1,80,000 TPA (+36%) and production transitioned to 100% Alu-Zinc, placing the Company among the select Indian manufacturers with complete Alu-Zinc coating capability; the project was commissioned in December 2025. Three growth projects are under implementation. A second colour coating line adds 1,50,000 TPA, taking total colour coating capacity from 86,000 TPA to 2,36,000 TPA (+174%, described elsewhere as 2.7 times) on an approved investment of Rs 65 crore, with commissioning targeted for Q2 FY27 - it removes the bottleneck on an existing line running at 97.2% utilisation. A 7 MW captive solar power project at Kutch, Gujarat, costing Rs 30 crore, is also targeted for Q2 FY27 and is expected to offset around 50%-55% of grid power dependency, cut effective power costs by nearly 40% and generate annual savings of Rs 7 crore to Rs 7.5 crore while supporting lower-CBAM-impact products for Europe. An enterprise-wide Salesforce CRM implementation is in progress. Beyond these, the roadmap is to progress a 3,60,000 MTPA Cold Rolling Mill complex targeted for FY28 at an estimated Rs 200 crore - shifting the primary raw material from cold-rolled coil to hot-rolled coil, incorporating a process acid recycling facility and reducing dependence on a concentrated supplier base - followed by a second Alu-Zinc line, with Alu-Zinc utilisation to be raised to 80%-85% along the way.

Honest that the YoY volume dip is ramp-timing, and that a precise 12% FY27 margin can't be pinned. Credible on the back-to-back cost-insulation model.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Focused specialisation: rather than pursuing breadth, the Company has deepened expertise in coated steel, building a business defined by technical excellence and agile execution
- Structural logistics advantage - Kutch plant located around 50 km from the Kandla and Mundra ports, enabling cost-effective domestic and international dispatch
- Proprietary coated-steel brands (Colour Strong, Zingalvo, Singham) developed for distinct market segments
- Established export franchise across more than 22 countries with deepening relationships in Europe, Africa and the Middle East, reinforced by long-term supply agreements with marquee European clients
- Ability to deliver customised solutions in smaller order quantities without compromising quality or service, combined with strong relationships with global OEMs
- Premium product positioning - Alu-Zinc coated steel commands a premium of Rs 3,000 to Rs 5,000 per tonne over conventional galvanised steel
- Improving financial profile recognised externally, with Acuite upgrading the long-term rating to A from A- and the short-term rating to A1 from A2
- Accredited quality and safety systems (BIS, ISO 9001/14001/45001) supporting export acceptance

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Compete on value rather than volume alone - premiumisation is at the core of the strategy, with a portfolio spanning Alu-Zinc coated steel coils and sheets and pre-painted steel coils and sheets
- Move up the value chain by shifting sales mix towards pre-painted and Alu-Zinc coated products (pre-painted steel was 80.44% of sales, up from 74.49%)
- Expand value-added capacity - second colour coating line and a proposed second Aluminium-Zinc line
- Strengthen backward integration through a planned Cold Rolling Mill complex that shifts primary raw material from cold-rolled coil to hot-rolled coil, …
